claims.text: British Library catalogue; Sikkim Court English edition

The British Library catalogues Patna revenue-council consultations. Sikkim’s English edition reproduces Sugauli’s Kali–Rapti lowlands clause between Nepal’s ruler and the East India Company, with 1815 text and 1816 exchange. These establish neither blanket annexation, Patna’s transfer nor today’s disputed boundary; full Patna hierarchy remains unproved.
Which selected record actually names a territorial cession? Sugauli territorial clause naming Kali–Rapti lowlands

claims.text: Which named territorial example does Sugauli supply, and what separate institution does the Patna catalogue describe? The clause names Kali–Rapti lowlands; the other witness catalogues a Patna Provincial Council of Revenue. It does not establish a Patna cession or full Bengal/Bihar hierarchy.

The 1815 text/1816 exchange in a modern Sikkim English edition supplies a named Kali–Rapti lowlands clause, not blanket Nepal annexation or current boundary adjudication. The separate Patna revenue institution is catalogued; full Bengal/Bihar hierarchy is unproved. No Madhesi/Tharu/community rights or consent follows from state parties.
